title: Gifts of the Spirit are given so that all may benefit
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Kirtland, Ohio, around 8 March 1831. The day in the earliest copy is hard to read but is probably the 8th. Members had begun keeping unbelievers out of their meetings, and some questioned the practice. Joseph had also met spiritual displays in the Ohio branches that he judged unsound. The revelation addressed both concerns for the whole Church.
summary: The revelation says elders should lead meetings as the Holy Spirit directs. It forbids casting anyone out of public meetings. Earnest seekers who are not members may stay in sacrament and confirmation meetings. Members who have sinned should not take the sacrament until they make reconciliation. It warns against deception and tells members to “seek ye earnestly the best gifts”. It then lists gifts of the Spirit, from knowing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God to interpreting tongues. The bishop and appointed elders are to discern these gifts. It closes by asking that all be done in Christ’s name, with thanks.

contextNote.title: Why the gifts are sought
contextNote.text: The Ohio branches had seen spiritual displays that Joseph judged false. Verse 7 names the danger: being “seduced by evil spirits,” or by human commandments. Verse 8 gives the defense: seek the best gifts and remember why they are given. Verse 9 states that reason: they bless those who love God and keep his commandments. They are not given for “a sign” or for selfish use. Verses 11–12 add that no one has every gift, so each gift serves others. Here, to seek a gift means to seek something for the good of the whole church.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 46–48, “Seek Ye Earnestly the Best Gifts,” invites members to seek spiritual gifts. Which gift in verses 13–25 might you seek, and how would it serve others as verse 26 says?
reviewNote: Read all 33 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 8 March 1831, to the Church, on conduct of meetings and spiritual gifts. JSP dates it circa 8 March because the day in Revelation Book 1 is obscured. JSP notes Joseph’s 4 March 1831 letter about “regulating” the Ohio churches. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
